mainTopic: Tests for a cracked clay pot, limbs and extra fingers in טומאה, מדרס versus טמא מת, and who may judge or testify.
overview: This amud covers several short topics. First, a ברייתא gives tests for a cracked clay pot: does the crack let liquid in (כונס משקה) or only seep out (מוציא משקה)? רבי יהודה floods an upside-down pot or sets it on a fire. רבי יוסי uses hot ash instead of fire, and steady dripping is also a sign. עולא explains that the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה disagree about water that gets in only by force. Next the גמרא explains lines of the משנה. A limb with a nail spreads טומאה even through an אהל. An extra finger with a bone but no nail does not, unless it lines up with the other fingers. Anything fit for מדרס can get טמא מת, but measuring containers like a סאה get only טמא מת, since they are not meant for sitting. Then two new משניות follow. A ממזר and a גר may judge money cases but not capital cases, and each one needs its own source. Someone blind in one eye may testify but may not judge, and the גמרא begins to ask whose opinion this follows.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's test: turn the pot upside down and flood it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says to turn the pot upside down and pour water over it. If water gets in, the crack is כונס משקה. If not, it is only מוציא משקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Turn the pot over, handles down, and flood it with water. If water comes in, we know the crack lets liquid in. If not, we know it only lets liquid out.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second opinion. רבי יהודה gives his own way to test the crack in a clay pot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two kinds of crack matter here: one big enough to let liquid IN (כונס), and a smaller one that only lets liquid seep OUT (מוציא). רבי יהודה's test puts the pot upside down and pours water over it. If water still gets inside, the crack is the bigger kind.

keyTerms.meaning: Lets liquid in. This is the bigger kind of crack.
Lets liquid out only. This is the smaller kind of crack.
The 'ears' of a pot, meaning its handles
Floods, pours water over
It is known, it is clear

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two results. 'Lets in' (כונס) is the BIGGER crack. 'Lets out only' (מוציא) is the smaller one. Liquid seeps out more easily than it gets in.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One bends the handles of the pot into it
phrases.notes: Literally 'bends the ears of the pot.' He means turning the pot upside down into the tub.

phrases.english: and floods water over it,
and if it lets [water] in —
it is known that it lets liquid in,
and if not —
it is known that it only lets liquid out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different test from the תנא קמא's test, which appears just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Turn the pot upside down and flood it with water. If water enters, it is כונס משקה. If not, it is only מוציא משקה.

steps.title: A second test: put the pot on the fire
steps.stepSummary: Another option is to set the pot, with liquid inside, on the fire. If the fire stops the leak, the crack is only מוציא משקה. If not, it is כונס משקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or put it on the fire. If the fire holds the liquid back, we know the crack only lets liquid out. If not, we know it lets liquid in.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second way to test the same crack, this time using heat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heat of the fire can seal a small crack and stop the seeping. If the fire stops the leak, the crack is small (מוציא). If the liquid keeps leaking even on the fire, the crack is big (כונס).

keyTerms.meaning: Sets it (the pot) on the fire
Fire
Holds it back, stops the leak

phrases.english: Or he sets it on the fire,
if the fire holds it back —
phrases.notes: He means the heat stops the liquid from seeping out through the crack.

phrases.english: it is known that it only lets liquid out,
and if not —
it is known that it lets liquid in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second testing method alongside the water test.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the fire stops the leak, the crack is מוציא משקה. If not, it is מכניס משקה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: use hot ash, not fire
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי rejects the fire test because fire is too strong. It could stop even a big crack. He uses hot ash (רמץ) instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Do not even put it on the fire, because the fire holds it back. Rather, put it on hot ash. If the ash holds it back, we know it only lets liquid out. If not, we know it lets liquid in.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי argues with the fire test from Step 2 and swaps in a gentler heat source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His worry is that a strong fire can stop a leak even when the crack is big. Then a כונס pot would wrongly be judged מוציא. Hot ash gives milder heat, so it only stops a truly small crack.

keyTerms.meaning: Hot ash or embers. It gives gentler heat than a fire.
Not even, not at all
Rather, instead

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף לֹא שׁוֹפְתָהּ עַל גַּבֵּי הָאוּר,
phrases.english: one should not even set it on the fire,
because the fire holds it back,
rather, he sets it on hot ash.
If the hot ash holds it back —
it is known that it only lets liquid out,
and if not —
it is known that it lets liquid in.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אַף לֹא שׁוֹפְתָהּ עַל גַּבֵּי הָאוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the fire test of Step 2 and replaces it with hot ash.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Test on hot ash, not fire. If the ash stops the leak, the crack is מוציא. If not, it is כונס.

steps.title: A sign: dripping drop after drop
steps.stepSummary: If the pot drips one drop after another, the crack is clearly the bigger kind, כונס משקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was dripping drop after drop, we know it lets liquid in.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one more simple sign for telling a big crack from a small one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dripping in steady drops shows the crack is more than a slow seep. That means it is big enough to count as כונס משקה. No fire or ash test is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Drips steadily
Drop after drop

steps.whatToRemember: All of these tests answer one question: is the crack big enough to let liquid IN (כונס), or does it only let liquid seep OUT (מוציא)?

phrases.english: If it was dripping drop after drop —
it is known that it lets liquid in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further sign to the tests already given.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Steady dripping, drop after drop, shows the crack is כונס משקה.

steps.title: What is the difference between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the תנא קמא's test (pot in a tub of water) and רבי יהודה's test (pot turned over and flooded).
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference is there between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finished, and now the גמרא starts its own discussion. It asks what the two water tests really disagree about. This sets up עולא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both tests use water to see whether liquid gets in, so they look almost the same. The גמרא wants to know when the two methods would give different results.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between...?
The first תנא, whose opinion opens the ברייתא without a name

phrases.english: What is there between
the first tanna and Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין תַּנָּא קַמָּא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from quoting the ברייתא to analyzing it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between the תנא קמא's tub test and רבי יהודה's upside-down flooding test.

steps.title: עולא: they disagree about water forced in
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that the two disagree about water that gets in only by force (כינוס על ידי הדחק). רבי יהודה does not count that, so he uses a gentler test.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The difference between them is liquid that comes in only by force.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question from Step 5 by pointing to the exact issue the two opinions argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pushing a pot down into a tub of water can force water through a crack that would not normally let liquid in. רבי יהודה holds that forced entry does not count as כונס, so he rejects the תנא קמא's method and uses his own. The תנא קמא counts water that gets in even under that pressure.

keyTerms.meaning: Liquid coming in
By force, under pressure
This is the difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא and רבי יהודה differ only on whether water that comes in by force counts as 'letting liquid in.'

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Liquid coming in by force
is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: כִּינּוּס עַל יְדֵי הַדְּחָק אִיכָּא בֵינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about whether water that gets in only under pressure counts as כונס משקה. רבי יהודה says it does not.

steps.title: A limb with a nail versus a limb with only a bone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a limb with a nail. It explains that a limb with a nail spreads טומאה in all three ways: touching, carrying, and אהל. A limb with a bone but no nail spreads it only by touching and carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Any limb that has a nail, and so on.' This means: if the limb has a nail, it makes things impure by touching, by carrying, and by being under one roof with them. If it has a bone but no nail, it makes things impure by touching and by carrying, but not by being under one roof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new line in the משנה and explains what difference a nail makes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A nail shows that this is a full, complete limb. A full limb spreads טומאה in every way, even through an אהל, even if it is smaller than a כזית. With only a bone and no nail, it is not treated as a full limb for אהל, so it spreads טומאה only by מגע and משא.

keyTerms.meaning: A nail (fingernail or toenail)
A limb or body part
A bone
Touching and carrying, two ways טומאה spreads
Impurity that spreads to people and things under the same roof as the source

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a limb with only a bone is pure. It still makes things impure by touching and carrying. The only thing it lacks is spreading טומאה through an אהל.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אֵבֶר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ צִפּוֹרֶן וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Any limb that has a nail, etc.
If it has a nail,
it makes things impure by touching, by carrying, and through a tent;

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ בּוֹ עֶצֶם וְאֵין בּוֹ צִפּוֹרֶן —
phrases.english: if it has a bone but has no nail,
it makes things impure by touching and by carrying
but does not make things impure through a tent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the cracked pot discussion and starts explaining the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A limb with a nail spreads טומאה by מגע, משא, and אהל. A limb with a bone and no nail spreads it only by מגע and משא.

steps.title: An extra finger with a bone but no nail
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא quotes his great teacher: an extra finger with a bone but no nail spreads טומאה by touching and carrying, but not through an אהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Our great teacher said this, may God help him. An extra finger that has a bone but no nail makes things impure by touching and by carrying, but not through a tent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא reports a ruling of his great teacher, רב, that applies the משנה's rule to a real case: an extra finger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think any finger counts as a full limb, even without a nail. רב חסדא teaches that an extra finger with no nail follows the משנה's rule for a bone without a nail. So it does not spread טומאה through an אהל.

keyTerms.meaning: An extra finger
'Our great teacher', here meaning רב
'May God help him', a blessing for the teacher

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
This matter was said by our great teacher,
may God be his help.
An extra finger that has a bone
but has no nail,
makes things impure by touching and by carrying,
but does not make things impure through a tent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: דָּבָר זֶה רַבֵּינוּ הַגָּדוֹל אֲמָרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משנה's bone-without-nail rule to an extra finger.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An extra finger with a bone but no nail spreads טומאה by מגע and משא, but not by אהל.

steps.title: Only when the extra finger is out of line with the others
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן limits the extra finger ruling that רב חסדא reported from his teacher. It applies only when the extra finger does not line up with the other fingers on the back of the hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: And this is only when the extra finger cannot be counted along the back of the hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a condition that narrows the extra finger ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the extra finger sits out of line, it needs a nail to count as a full limb. But if it lines up with the other fingers, it is treated like any regular finger. Then it spreads טומאה through an אהל even without a nail.

keyTerms.meaning: Counted, here meaning lined up in the row of fingers
The back of the hand

steps.whatToRemember: Extra finger with no nail: if it is out of line, there is no טומאה through אהל. If it lines up with the other fingers, it counts as a regular limb.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
And that is when it is not counted along the back of the hand.
phrases.notes: He means the extra finger is not in line with the row of fingers. If it is in line, it counts as a real finger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב חסדא's ruling to an extra finger that is out of line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra finger ruling applies only when the finger is not lined up with the others. A lined-up finger counts as a full limb.

steps.title: Whatever can become impure through treading can become impure from a corpse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and explains it. Anything fit to become impure through מדרס is also fit to become impure through טמא מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Anything that becomes impure through treading, and so on.' This means: anything that is fit for treading becomes impure with the impurity of a corpse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another line of the משנה and explains what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מדרס is the טומאה a זב passes on by sitting, lying, or leaning on an item made for that use. The גמרא explains the משנה's wording: the item does not need to have actually become impure through מדרס. If it is fit for מדרס, it can also become impure from a corpse.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity a זב passes on by treading, sitting, or lying on an item
Impurity that comes from a dead body
That is fit or suitable

phrases.english: Anything that becomes impure through treading, etc.
Anything that is fit for treading
becomes impure with corpse impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the limb discussion and explains a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any item fit to become impure through מדרס can become impure through טמא מת.

steps.title: What does the second half of the מדרס line come to include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the rest of the משנה's line: some things become impure through טמא מת but not through מדרס. It asks which items this means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה continues: some things can become impure from a dead body but cannot become impure from a זב sitting or treading on them. The גמרא asks: what items is this meant to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second half of the משנה line from Step 10 and asks which objects it is talking about. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 taught that anything fit for מדרס is also fit for טמא מת. Now the משנה says the reverse is not always true. The גמרא wants a real example of an object that gets טמא מת but never מדרס.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To include what?' The גמרא asks which case a phrase is meant to add

phrases.english: And there are things that become impure with corpse impurity
but do not become impure through treading.
phrases.notes: 'Treading' means a זב sitting or stepping on the item. That is מדרס.

phrases.english: What does this come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה line that Step 10 began
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete example of an item that becomes impure through טמא מת but not through מדרס

steps.title: Answer: measuring containers like a סאה and a תרקב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the line includes measuring containers such as a סאה or a תרקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include a סאה measure and a תרקב measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The משנה means measuring containers like a סאה or a תרקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These containers are real vessels, so they can become impure from a dead body. But they are made for measuring, not for sitting, so they cannot get מדרס impurity. The next step brings a source for this.

keyTerms.meaning: A standard measuring container for dry goods
A measuring container holding half a סאה

phrases.english: To include a se'a measure and a half-se'a measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Measuring containers (a סאה and a תרקב) become impure through טמא מת but not through מדרס

steps.title: A ברייתא proves that only seats get מדרס impurity
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that only an object made for sitting gets מדרס impurity. A measuring container is left out, since people would tell the sitter to get up so they can use it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: the פסוק says 'And he who sits on the object.' You might think that if a זב turned over a סאה or a תרקב and sat on it, it becomes impure. So the פסוק says 'on which the זב sits.' This means something set aside for sitting. It leaves out an item where we would tell the person: 'Get up, so we can do our work with it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove the answer from Step 12. The ברייתא uses the wording of a פסוק to show that a measuring container cannot get מדרס impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'on which the זב sits' show the item must be meant for sitting. A turned-over measuring container is still mainly a work tool. People would ask the sitter to stand up so they could use it, so it never counts as a seat.

keyTerms.meaning: Turned upside down
'The פסוק teaches.' It introduces the words that settle the question
A man with a certain bodily flow who is impure and can pass on impurity
Set aside for sitting. Its main use is as a seat

steps.whatToRemember: An object becomes impure through מדרס only if it is mainly meant for sitting or lying. A tool that is sometimes sat on, like an upside-down measuring container, does not count. It can still become impure from a dead body.
steps.confusionAlert: The measuring container does not stop being a כלי. It is still a vessel and can become impure from a dead body. It is left out only from the special rules of מדרס.

phrases.english: As it is taught: "And he who sits on the object,"
one might think that if he turned over a se'a measure and sat on it,
or a half-se'a measure and sat on it,
it should become impure?
So the verse says: "on which the zav sits"
meaning something set aside for sitting,
which leaves out this item, where we say to him:
Get up, so we can do our work.
phrases.notes: The owners need the container back for measuring, so it is not really a seat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the answer in Step 12
steps.raayaObject: That a סאה and a תרקב cannot become impure through מדרס
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ויקרא 15:6, 'on which the זב sits', as limited to objects meant for sitting
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic test for מדרס: what the object is mainly used for, not whether someone happened to sit on it.

steps.title: New משנה: who may judge capital cases and money cases
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה uses the same pattern for judges. Whoever is fit to judge דיני נפשות is fit to judge דיני ממונות, but some are fit for money cases and not for capital cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Anyone fit to judge capital cases is fit to judge money cases. But some people are fit to judge money cases and not capital cases.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It uses the same 'all X are Y, but some Y are not X' pattern, now applied to judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules for judging דיני נפשות are stricter than for דיני ממונות. So anyone who passes the stricter test also passes the easier one. Some people pass only the easier one. The גמרא will next explain who those people are.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. It marks the start of the משנה text
Capital cases, where a life is at stake
Money cases

phrases.english: MISHNA: Anyone fit to judge capital cases
is fit to judge money cases,
and there are those fit to judge money cases
who are not fit to judge capital cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי' כׇּל הָרָאוּי לָדוּן דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה that uses the same pattern as the earlier lines
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fitness to judge דיני נפשות includes fitness to judge דיני ממונות, but not the reverse

steps.title: רב יהודה: The משנה's line includes a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that the משנה's line 'some are fit for money cases but not capital cases' comes to include a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: this line comes to include a ממזר. He may judge money cases, but not capital cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רב יהודה telling us who the משנה means when it says some people may judge money cases but not capital cases. His answer is a ממזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (step 14) said there are people who may judge דיני ממונות but not דיני נפשות, without saying who. רב יהודה fills in the case: a ממזר may judge money cases, but not capital cases.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
To include; to bring in an extra case
A child born from a forbidden relationship, such as incest or adultery

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Yehuda said:
It comes to include a mamzer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which person the משנה in step 14 has in mind.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ממזר may judge דיני ממונות but not דיני נפשות.

steps.title: This was already taught in another משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a משנה in סנהדרין already teaches this, and רב יהודה already explained that one as including a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned this once: 'All are fit to judge money cases, but not all are fit to judge capital cases.' We asked what that comes to include, and רב יהודה said: a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה. Another משנה already teaches the same rule, and he already used it to include a ממזר, so why would our משנה repeat it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is that the same lesson seems to appear twice. A משנה should not repeat itself for no reason, so if both sources teach about a ממזר, one of them looks extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone is fit (qualified)
We already learned this once. It introduces a repetition challenge
And we discussed it; we raised a question about it

phrases.english: We already learned this one time:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in סנהדרין.

phrases.english: All are fit to judge money cases,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרִין לָדוּן דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת.
phrases.english: but not all are fit to judge capital cases.
And we discussed it: what does 'all' come to include?
And Rav Yehuda said: it comes to include a mamzer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 15 by arguing that it makes our משנה repeat a lesson already taught.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's reading of our משנה as including a ממזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same lesson about a ממזר is already taught in another משנה, so teaching it here would be a repetition.

steps.title: One source includes a גר, the other a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two sources are not the same: one comes to include a גר and the other a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: One source comes to include a convert, and the other comes to include a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by splitting the job between the two sources. Each one adds a different person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is repeated after all. One source teaches that a גר may judge money cases, and the other teaches the same about a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert to Judaism
One... and the other

phrases.english: One comes to include a convert,
and the other comes to include a mamzer.

steps.triggerLanguage: חדא לאתויי גר וחדא לאתויי ממזר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the repetition challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two sources so each teaches a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources teach about a ממזר, so one is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: One source teaches about a גר and the other about a ממזר.

steps.title: Why the גר case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to show that both cases are needed. If we only learned about a גר, we might think it is because he may marry into the community, which a ממזר may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If we only learned about a convert, we would say he is allowed because he may marry into the community. But a ממזר, who may not marry into the community, we would say is not allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is defending its answer by showing that both lessons are necessary. This step gives the first half: the גר case alone would not teach us about a ממזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גר has a strong point in his favor: he may marry into the Jewish community. A ממזר lacks this, so from the גר case alone we might wrongly think a ממזר may not judge even money cases.

keyTerms.meaning: And both are needed
For if it had taught us (only this)
Allowed to 'enter the community,' meaning to marry a Jew of regular lineage
I would say no (it does not apply)

phrases.english: And both are needed,
for if it had taught us only about a convert —
that is because he is fit to enter the community,
phrases.notes: This means he may marry a regular Jewish woman.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מַמְזֵר דְּאֵין רָאוּי לָבֹא בַּקָּהָל,
phrases.english: but a mamzer, who is not fit to enter the community,
I would say he may not judge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 17 by showing the ממזר lesson is not learned from the גר lesson.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: shows each case is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Learning only about a גר, one might exclude a ממזר, since he may not marry into the community.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ממזר case must be taught separately.

steps.title: Why the ממזר case alone would not be enough, so both are needed
steps.stepSummary: If we only learned about a ממזר, we might think it is because he comes from Jewish parents, which a גר does not. So both cases must be taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if we only learned about a ממזר, we would say he is allowed because he comes from Jewish parents. But a convert, who comes from non-Jewish parents, we would say is not allowed. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second half of the proof and concludes that both lessons are necessary. The ממזר case alone would not teach us about a גר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ממזר has his own point in his favor: he was born to Jewish parents. A גר lacks this. Since each case has a reason to be lenient that the other lacks, neither can be learned from the other, and both sources are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'fit drop,' meaning born from Jewish parents
An 'unfit drop,' meaning born from non-Jewish parents
It is needed (both teachings are necessary)

steps.whatToRemember: Both a גר and a ממזר may judge money cases but not capital cases. Each needs its own source: a גר may marry into the community, and a ממזר comes from Jewish parents. Neither case can be learned from the other.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only about a mamzer —
that is because he comes from a fit drop,
phrases.notes: He was born to Jewish parents, even though the relationship was forbidden.

phrases.english: but a convert, who comes from an unfit drop —
phrases.notes: He was born to non-Jewish parents.

phrases.english: I would say he may not judge,
so both are needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 18 and closes the answer to step 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both sources are needed, one for a גר and one for a ממזר, because each has a reason to be lenient that the other lacks.

steps.title: משנה: Every judge can be a witness, but not every witness can be a judge
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that anyone fit to judge is fit to testify, but some people are fit to testify and not to judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Anyone who is fit to judge is fit to testify. But there are some people who are fit to testify and are not fit to judge.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a rule comparing judges and witnesses. Judging has stricter requirements than testifying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule runs only one way: being a judge requires everything a witness needs, and more. The second half, 'there are some fit to testify but not to judge', is vague because it does not say who these people are. That is exactly what the גמרא will ask next.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit, qualified
To judge, to serve as a judge in a case
To testify, to serve as a witness

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as 'judges and witnesses have the same rules.' Every judge can be a witness, but not every witness can be a judge.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: Anyone who is fit to judge
is fit to testify,
and there are some who are fit to testify
but are not fit to judge.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי' כׇּל הַכָּשֵׁר לָדוּן כָּשֵׁר לְהָעִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה, but with the same pattern as the earlier משנה in step 14 ('some are fit for X but not for Y').
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone fit to judge is fit to testify; some are fit to testify but not to judge.

steps.title: Who is included by 'fit to testify but not to judge'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the second half of the משנה comes to add.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who the משנה means by 'some are fit to testify but not to judge.' This is a clarifying question that sets up רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה hints at a group of people without naming them. The גמרא wants a concrete example of someone who may be a witness but may not be a judge. It is the same kind of 'what does this include?' question asked in step 11 about the מדרס line.

keyTerms.meaning: To include, to bring in an extra case
What?

phrases.english: GEMARA: What does this come to include?
phrases.notes: 'This' is the משנה's line about people fit to testify but not to judge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the vague second half of the משנה in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of person is fit to testify but not fit to judge.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: It includes someone blind in one eye
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the line includes a person blind in one eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: It comes to include a person who is blind in one of his eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the example the גמרא asked for: someone blind in one eye may testify but may not judge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the משנה's vague line has a concrete case. A person blind in one eye is still a valid witness, but he is not allowed to sit as a judge. The גמרא has not yet said where this rule comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: A blind person
In one of his eyes

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
To include one who is blind in one of his eyes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְאֵתוֹיֵי סוֹמֵא בְּאַחַת מֵעֵינָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The line includes a person blind in one eye: valid as a witness, not valid as a judge.

steps.title: Whose opinion does this follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that a person blind in one eye may not judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: And whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which sage holds this rule about a person blind in one eye. This is a setup line: the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's answer means the משנה holds that a person blind in one eye may not judge. The גמרא now wants to tie that rule to a specific תנא, which suggests not everyone agrees with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? Whose opinion is this?

phrases.english: And whose opinion is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רבי יוחנן's answer by asking which תנא it matches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The name of the תנא who holds that one blind in one eye is unfit to judge.
